questions.question: The first musician to be awarded with the highest civilian award of India, the ‘Bharat Ratna’ was __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MS Subbulakshmi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **MS Subbulakshmi** was the first musician to be awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 1998.
 
• She was a renowned Carnatic vocalist and was widely recognized as the "Queen of Music."
 
• MS Subbulakshmi's contributions to Indian classical music were unparalleled, and she played a crucial role in popularizing the genre both in India and abroad.
 
• She was also the first Indian musician to perform at the United Nations General Assembly, further highlighting her international acclaim.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award of the Republic of India, instituted in 1954.
 
• It is awarded in recognition of exceptional service/performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavor.
 
• The award was originally limited to achievements in the arts, literature, science, and public services, but the government expanded its scope to include any field of human endeavor in December 2011.
 
• Recipients of the Bharat Ratna receive a Sanad (certificate) signed by the President of India and a medallion.
 
• The medallion is in the shape of a peepal leaf and is made of toned bronze.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that every religious denomination or section shall have the right to own and acquire movable and immovable property?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 26(c)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 26(c) of the Indian Constitution states that every religious denomination or any section thereof shall have the right to own and acquire movable and immovable property.
 
• This provision ensures that religious groups can possess and manage property to maintain their religious and charitable institutions.
 
• The right under Article 26 is subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
• Article 26 is a part of the fundamental rights guaranteed under Part III of the Indian Constitution, specifically providing cultural and educational rights to religious and linguistic minorities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• Part III of the Constitution, which includes Articles 12 to 35, deals with Fundamental Rights.
 
• Article 26 falls under the category of the right to freedom of religion, which is crucial for maintaining the secular fabric of the nation.

questions.question: Under which Schedule of the Indian Constitution is the form of oath or affirmation for a Judge of the Supreme Court mentioned?

• The Third Schedule also includes forms of oath or affirmation for other constitutional positions such as the President, Vice-President, Ministers, Members of Parliament, and Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.
 
• Taking an oath or affirmation is a mandatory requirement before assuming office for these constitutional positions.
 
• The oath or affirmation signifies the commitment to uphold the Constitution and discharge duties faithfully and impartially.

• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**

• Chilika Lake is known for its rich biodiversity and is a significant habitat for a variety of flora and fauna, including migratory birds.
 
• The lake is an important ecosystem and supports the livelihoods of local communities through fishing and tourism.
 
• Chilika Lake is also recognized as a Ramsar site, highlighting its importance as a wetland of international importance.

• The lake is home to several threatened species of plants and animals and serves as a wintering ground for migratory birds from the far reaches of Russia, Mongolia, and beyond.
 
• In addition to its ecological importance, Chilika Lake supports a vibrant fishing industry, providing livelihoods for thousands of fishermen and their families.
 
• The lake is also a popular tourist destination, attracting visitors with its scenic beauty, bird-watching opportunities, and boat tours.

questions.question: According to the Koppen climate classification system, ‘Am’ is the code for which type of climate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical monsoon climate**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Koppen climate classification system** is one of the most widely used climate classification systems.
 
• In this system, the code **'Am'** stands for **Tropical monsoon climate**.
 
• This type of climate is characterized by heavy rainfall during the monsoon season and a short dry season.
 
• Regions with this climate typically have lush vegetation and a high level of biodiversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Koppen climate classification system was developed by **Wladimir Koppen**, a German climatologist, in the early 20th century.
 
• The system categorizes climates based on annual and monthly averages of temperature and precipitation.
 
• It is widely used in environmental and ecological studies, as well as in geography and meteorology.
 
• Other major climate types in the Koppen system include **Tropical rainforest (Af)**, **Desert (B)**, and **Temperate (C)** climates.

• The Attorney-General represents the Government of India in all cases in the Supreme Court in which the Government of India is concerned.
 
• The position of the Attorney-General is not a full-time position, and the officeholder can practice privately as well, provided the other legal work does not conflict with the duties as Attorney-General.

questions.question: Flowerless plants, naked seeds, needle like leaves and cones as reproductive structure are the characteristics of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**gymnosperms**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gymnosperms** are characterized by flowerless plants, naked seeds, needle-like leaves, and cones as reproductive structures.
 
• They do not produce flowers or fruits, and their seeds are not enclosed within an ovary.
 
• Their leaves are typically shaped like needles or scales, which helps them reduce water loss.
 
• Examples of gymnosperms include pines, spruces, and firs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Gymnosperms are among the oldest living plants and have been around since the time of the dinosaurs.
 
• They are primarily found in cooler regions where they form large forests.
 
• Unlike angiosperms (flowering plants), gymnosperms do not have a wide variety of forms and structures.
 
• They play a crucial role in the ecosystem by providing habitat and food for various wildlife species.
 
• Gymnosperms are also economically important for timber, resin, and other products.

__
 
• The United Nations declared the World Physics Year, also known as the Einstein Year, in **2005** to mark the 100th anniversary of Albert Einstein's annus mirabilis (miracle year) when he published four groundbreaking papers.
 
• The year 2005 was chosen to celebrate Einstein's contributions to physics, including the theory of relativity and the photoelectric effect.
 
• The declaration aimed to promote physics education and awareness globally, highlighting the importance of physics in our daily lives and its contributions to technological advancements.
 
• Many events and activities were organized worldwide to commemorate this significant milestone in the history of science.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Albert Einstein** is one of the most renowned physicists in history, known for his contributions to the understanding of the fundamental laws of nature.
 
• His work laid the foundation for modern physics and has had a profound impact on various fields, including quantum mechanics and cosmology.
 
• Einstein received the **Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921** for his explanation of the photoelectric effect, which was crucial in the development of quantum theory.
 
• The year 2005 was also designated as the International Year of Physics (IYP) by UNESCO to coincide with the World Physics Year celebration.
